fixed.what: The option D analysis said USD 1.535 million came from one wrong maturity band, and gave two examples. Checked with python3: those examples give USD 1.098 million (commodity at 12%, credit equivalent 27.45) and USD 0.874 million (seven-year swap at 0.5%, credit equivalent 21.85). No single band misread gives 1.535, which implies a credit equivalent of about 38.4. The analysis now says this. The trap explanation's 'a wrong maturity band' was changed to 'a figure that needs add-ons larger than the grid assigns'. Key A (25.85 x 0.5 x 8% = 1.034) unchanged.

The option A analysis said 13.73% was consistent with applying only one or two of the four factor premia. Checked with python3: the risk-free rate plus any one correctly computed premium gives 8.00% to 12.10%, and plus any two gives 14.75% to 20.68%. Neither gives 13.73%. The analysis now says this. Key C (32.93%) unchanged.

The option B analysis said 86.2/13.8 came from weighting by beta alone or by the volatilities. Weighting by beta alone gives 47.4/52.6. 86.2% is exactly the normalised squared position weights: 0.7143^2/(0.7143^2+0.2857^2) = 0.5102/0.5918 = 0.8621 (python3). The option B analysis and the trap explanation now give this construction. Key D (w x beta: 69.3/30.7) unchanged.
